From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>

On Sun, Oct 3, 2027 at 2:05 PM Sara Holt <sara.holt@acmeanalytics.com> wrote:
> We’re seeing sustained latency spikes ...

Triage notes (initial):
- Confirmed: reserved pool for Acme (pool-acme-42) reports 100% GPU utilization on two nodes; queues building on dispatcher.
- Root candidate: a scheduling change rolled out earlier today (scheduler v2 tweak, commit ab12c3) that deprioritizes small-slice batching in favor of throughput heuristics. For workloads with high KV cache mutation and long context lengths the heuristic is causing larger-than-expected batch formation and KV cache churn.
- Observed significant KV cache growth for tenant acme-tenant-id leading to memory pressure and fallback to host memory causing slowdowns and 5xx OOMs.

Immediate mitigations I can apply now (low risk):
1) Route Acme to fallback quantized model variant (acme/fraud-v3-q4_0) on a less-loaded pool. ETA ~8 minutes to start draining.
2) Trigger targeted KV-cache eviction for acme-tenant-id to recover headroom (will drop warm cache; some latency spike for cold queries expected).
3) Roll back scheduler commit ab12c3 for affected clusters (risky; requires manual coordination).

I’ve opened JIRA INF-7112 (link above) and attached a diff for a hotfix to limit batch size for tenants with high cache churn (hotfix_patch.diff). Marcus: can you confirm if we have immediate capacity in hosted pools to accept burst traffic?

I’ll stand by to run the cache eviction and routing.

- Rafael
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Attachment: hotfix_patch.diff
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU headroom breach impacting Acme Analytics - incident update

Hi Sara — quick update and actions we’ve taken in the last 45 minutes: 

1) We routed a portion (~30%) of your traffic to a hosted fallback pool running the quantized variant acme/fraud-v3-q4_0 to immediately reduce latency; that routing is actively draining now.
2) We executed a targeted KV-cache eviction for your tenant at 08:50 PDT; this recovered ~12GB of GPU RAM and reduced OOMs.
3) Rafael has prepared a hotfix to limit batch growth; we are testing the patch in parallel.

Expected impact: latency should progressively return to normal within ~30–45 minutes after the routing takes full effect. We’ll monitor p50/p95 and 5xx closely and share live metrics.

We understand the SLA impact here and will propose a credit for the affected window. Monica will follow up on compensation and an actionable postmortem.

Can you confirm if there are any long-running jobs we should pause on your side to reduce load while we stabilize?

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep you updated every 15 minutes until this is resolved.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Manager, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
